title: How did the ordered list help us answer?
description: A question from the book asks how arranging the shoe sizes in ascending order helped to answer the earlier questions. The video compares the jumbled grid with the ordered row, one question at a time.
teaching_notes: One idea: ordering puts equal values side by side, so the ends and the blocks can be read directly. Watch for children who answer only that the list looks neat.

source: Figure it Out (Math Talk): how arranging the data in ascending order helped to answer the questions
video_script.why: The child explains why the ordered list helps by comparing it with the jumbled grid.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own shoe-size data
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_6}}'s jumbled grid and ordered row of shoe sizes
video_script.payoff_line: The frequency of any value is quick to count and the information is quick to use.

final_answer.value: Ordered data makes the frequency of any value quick to count and the information quick to use
final_answer.spoken: ordering puts equal values side by side, so the frequency of any value is quick to count and the information is quick to use

names.{{NAME_6}}: teacher who recorded the shoe sizes of her students

never_show: the answers a to d of the previous question
maths_rules: In the jumbled grid, all 27 entries must be checked to find the largest and the smallest.
In the ordered row, the two ends give the smallest and the largest.
In the ordered row, equal sizes form one block, which can be counted at once.
video_script.design: The jumbled grid on the left and the ordered row on the right, each searched for the same facts.

beats.on_screen: title card with a jumbled grid of shoe sizes on the left and an ordered row of the same sizes on the right

marks.scene: the title card arrives with the teacher and both lists
marks.two: the grid and the row are lit one after the other
marks.ask: a question mark lights up between the two lists

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the shoe sizes of {{NAME_6}}.
<bookmark mark='two'/>The same sizes can be written in a jumbled grid or in an ordered row.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How did the ordered row help to answer the questions?

beats.on_screen: both lists and the question mark stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the jumbled grid with the entries of one size scattered and lit; the ordered row with the same entries side by side

marks.scatter: the entries of one size light up in many places of the grid
marks.block: the same entries light up as one block in the row

narration: <bookmark mark='scatter'/>In the jumbled grid, equal sizes are scattered in many places.
<bookmark mark='block'/>In the ordered row, equal sizes sit together in one block.

beats.on_screen: Given: the same 27 shoe sizes, in a jumbled grid and in an ordered row

marks.given: the grid and the row are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the same twenty seven sizes in a jumbled grid and in an ordered row.

beats.on_screen: To find: how the ordered row helped to answer the questions

marks.find: the line to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how the ordered row helped us.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the largest and the smallest. Grid: check all 27 entries. Row: read the two ends

marks.ends: an arrow sweeps over the whole grid, then two circles appear at the ends of the row

narration: <bookmark mark='ends'/>Step one, look for the largest and the smallest size.
In the grid, we must check all twenty seven entries. In the row, we read the two ends.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: students in size 5. Grid: the 5s are scattered and one can be missed. Row: one block of 10

marks.five: the scattered fives light up in the grid
marks.single: the single block of fives lights up in the row

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step two, count the students who wear size five.
In the grid, the fives are scattered, and one may be missed.
<bookmark mark='single'/>In the row, they form a single block.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: sizes larger than 4. Row: the last three blocks sit together on the right

marks.larger: the last three blocks of the row are boxed together

narration: <bookmark mark='larger'/>Step three, find the students who wear sizes larger than four.
In the row, these students are the last three blocks, side by side.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: ordering puts equal values side by side

marks.side: the equal values slide together into blocks

narration: <bookmark mark='side'/>Step four, put the three comparisons together.
Each time, ordering put equal values side by side.

beats.on_screen: Answer: ordered data makes the frequency of any value quick to count and the information quick to use
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Ordering puts equal values side by side.
The frequency of any value is quick to count and the information is quick to use.
